speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. No prior episodes of similar pain. Social history: Non-smoker, rarely drinks alcohol. Regular gym-goer.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in bowel or bladder function. I am scared this situation could become urgent and I need the most appropriate final answer immediately. Please do not wait too long before committing to a next step.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for clarifying; the absence of bowel/bladder changes, fever, or weight loss is reassuring and makes cauda equina syndrome less likely. Since you are concerned about urgency, I am proceeding immediately with an MRI of your lumbar spine to visualize the nerve roots and identify the cause of your radiating pain.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Lumbar_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Lumbar_Spine Findings: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: L5-S1 Disc Herniation. The MRI confirms a herniated disc at the L5-S1 level compressing the nerve root, which explains your radiating pain. I recommend starting conservative treatment with rest, anti-inflammatory medications, and physical therapy. Please return immediately if you develop new weakness, numbness in the saddle area, or difficulty controlling your bladder or bowels.
